primitives.name: Data Isolation Boundary
primitives.verbatim_quote: Database needs: separate Postgres/MySQL per stateful app where required; never share production GSE DB.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'D_{app}': 'Distinct database instance per application', 'S_{state}': 'Stateful application component'}
primitives.assumptions: Each application requires independent persistence layer to prevent cross-contamination of data models and access patterns.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When shared database leads to race conditions or unauthorized data access.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a partition function in statistical mechanics where each application's data state is a distinct subsystem with unique entropy.
layer2.telemetry: Database connection logs, query latency variance across apps

primitives.name: Email Delivery Planning
primitives.verbatim_quote: Email/SMTP needs: listmonk and Chatwoot require deliverability planning; Twenty/Cap/Penpot need SMTP for invites or auth flows.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'E_{deliver}': 'Email delivery success rate', 'S_{smtp}': 'SMTP configuration parameter set', 'T_{auth}': 'Authentication token lifecycle'}
primitives.assumptions: Email systems must be provisioned with deliverability metrics and secure credential handling to avoid spam classification.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When deliverability drops below threshold due to misconfigured MX records or rate limiting.

layer2.mapping: Kernel of email reliability is derived from SMTP transaction log consistency and domain reputation tracking.
layer2.telemetry: Delivery status reports, bounce rates, SPF/DKIM validation logs

primitives.name: Auth SSO Enforcement
primitives.verbatim_quote: Auth/SSO needs: start with private admin auth, then OIDC/Google/Microsoft only after redirect URLs and owner approval.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'A_{admin}': 'Private administrative access control', 'A_{sso}': 'Single sign-on provider integration', 'R_{url}': 'Redirect URL policy enforcement'}
primitives.assumptions: Access control must evolve incrementally to maintain auditability and reduce attack surface during integration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Upon unauthorized redirection or unapproved identity provider inclusion.

layer2.mapping: Isomorphic to a cryptographic key exchange protocol where access tokens are issued under strict redirect policies.
layer2.telemetry: Login event timestamps, SSO provider registration logs, redirect URL compliance checks

The three core primitives—data isolation, email delivery planning, and auth SSO enforcement—are foundational to a resilient cross-stack architecture. Data isolation ensures that each service maintains its own persistent state without interference, modeled as a partitioned system akin to thermodynamic subsystems. Email delivery planning introduces probabilistic reliability constraints tied to network-level configurations and reputation management, forming a kernel of trust. Auth SSO enforcement enforces a temporal and conditional access lattice, where privilege escalation is gated by policy compliance. These primitives collectively define a failure space where breaches occur at the boundary between layers, particularly when data sharing, deliverability, or access control policies are violated. The risk profile is minimized through layered observability and controlled expansion of service interdependencies.
